stories.title: Selldorf Architects Signs Long-Term Renewal at 860 Broadway
stories.excerpt: Colliers SVP Seth Hecht has secured a 10-year, 13,815-square-foot lease renewal for architecture firm Selldorf Architects at 860 Broadway. Hecht represented Gordon Property Group in completing the long-term renewal transaction. Selldorf Architects was represented by Erik Schmall and Scott Weiss of Savills. Led by internationally acclaimed architect Annabelle Selldorf, the firm has called 860 Broadway home for the past two decades. “860 Broadway is one of Manhattan’s iconic office buildings, and its location continues to make it a highly desirable destination for creative and innovative companies,” said Hecht. “When a firm as globally respected as Selldorf Architects commits to another decade in the building, it speaks to both the property’s enduring appeal and the long-term strength of this market.” In addition to Selldorf Architects, current 860 Broadway tenants include Industrious, Valon and retail tenant Uniqlo. Hecht is also representing Gordon Property Group in leasing three additional Manhattan office properties. The post Selldorf Architects Signs Long-Term Renewal at 860 Broadway appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Selldorf Architects renews 13,815 SF at 860 Broadway, Manhattan, 10-year term
Architecture firm commits for two additional decades in Flatiron District location
Long-term renewal signals sustained demand for creative-class office in Manhattan
stories.summary: Architecture firm Selldorf Architects renewed its 10-year lease for 13,815 square feet at Gordon Property Group's 860 Broadway in Manhattan's Flatiron District, where it has been based for 20 years. The renewal was brokered by Colliers (Seth Hecht for landlord) and Savills. The lease represents sustained tenant commitment to Manhattan office despite broader market uncertainty, signaling continued viability of Class-A creative office in premium submarkets.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. Office renewal validates that Manhattan's creative/design-class tenant base remains stable, suggesting continued professional-services employment and resident base retention in adjacent residential markets like Flatiron/NoMad; however, this is a trailing indicator, not a leading demand signal for apartment development.

stories.title: Innocean USA Signs 100K-SF lease with Hackman Capital in Headquarters Relocation
stories.excerpt: Advertising agency Innocean USA has signed a new 101,000-square-foot office lease at Hackman Capital Partners’ 888 N. Douglas property in El Segundo.  The space will serve as the company’s U.S. headquarters and represents a relocation from 50,000 square feet of space in Huntington Beach. The tenant will move into its new space after construction concludes in 2027. JLL’s Jason Fine, Jeff Ingham, and Mitch Lundquist represented Innocean USA in the new lease. Hackman Capital represented itself. “This is a transformative change for Innocean USA, and we spent years advising the leadership team to help find a ‘one of one’ facility that would bring their company vision of the future to reality,” said Fine. “This is going to be a special place where their employees and creativity will absolutely thrive.” Across from the Lakers’ practice facility and the L.A. Times headquarters, 888 Douglas is a 30-acre campus with four buildings totaling approximately 550,000 square feet. Hackman Capital purchased the 1930s-era aerospace manufacturing site in 2016 and invested $100 million to transform it into a creative office campus. The post Innocean USA Signs 100K-SF lease with Hackman Capital in Headquarters Relocation appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Innocean USA HQ relocation: 101K SF at 888 Douglas, El Segundo; move-in 2027
Doubles footprint from 50K SF Huntington Beach; ~600 employee transfer planned
Hackman Capital 30-acre creative campus attracts major tenant expansion and talent consolidation
stories.summary: Advertising agency Innocean USA signed a 101,000-square-foot lease at Hackman Capital Partners' 888 Douglas creative office campus in El Segundo, representing a relocation and doubling of its U.S. headquarters footprint from 50,000 square feet in Huntington Beach. The company will relocate approximately 600 employees and move in after construction concludes in 2027. The campus is a 30-acre, 550,000-square-foot former aerospace manufacturing site transformed by Hackman.
stories.impact: Significant demand signal for multifamily in Los Angeles South Bay / El Segundo submarket. A 600-person employer relocation consolidating from two locations signals near-term in-migration of white-collar workforce into El Segundo and surrounding LAX-adjacent corridors through 2027; multifamily developers should underwrite for rental demand from Innocean employees and talent attraction ripple, with best positioning in walkable mixed-use near 888 Douglas or along El Segundo commute corridors to Huntington Beach feeder market.

stories.title: MADDD Equities Scoops Up Vacant West Farms Industrial
stories.excerpt: Ariel Property Advisors closed the sale of 425 Devoe Ave., a vacant multi-story industrial property in the West Farms neighborhood of The Bronx, for $10,750,000. The property spans 60,000 square feet above grade, which translates to $180 per square foot, with an additional 30,000 square feet below grade. An Ariel investment sales team led by senior director Jason M. Gold, along with partner Sean R. Kelly, Esq. and director Daniel Mahfa represented the seller, Abingdon Square Partners. The buyer was MADDD Equities, LLC. “The sale of 425 Devoe Ave. demonstrates the strong demand for large, commercial sites offering convenient regional access,” said Gold. Situated on a 40,097-square-foot lot, the property features four levels of usable industrial and warehouse space. It is located near the 2 and 5 subway lines and offers convenient access to the Cross Bronx Expressway, Sheridan Boulevard and the broader New York region. The post MADDD Equities Scoops Up Vacant West Farms Industrial appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MADDD Equities acquires 60K SF vacant industrial, West Farms Bronx, for $10.75M
60K above-grade + 30K below-grade at 425 Devoe Ave.; $180/SF valuation
Large-site industrial demand near 2/5 subway, Cross Bronx Expressway access
stories.summary: Ariel Property Advisors closed the sale of 425 Devoe Ave., a vacant 60,000-square-foot above-grade multi-story industrial property in West Farms, Bronx, to MADDD Equities for $10.75 million ($180/SF). The property includes 30,000 SF below-grade and sits on a 40,097-SF lot with proximity to the 2 and 5 subway lines and Cross Bronx Expressway.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. However, the transaction signals appetite for large-format Bronx industrial sites with strong transit access; if MADDD intends conversion (e.g., to creative office, last-mile logistics, or—less likely—mixed-use residential), this could indicate Bronx industrial-to-mixed-use conversion pipeline worth monitoring for land banking or future development near transit hubs.

stories.title: Shopoff Secures Approval for Buena Park Residential Development
stories.excerpt: Shopoff Realty Investments has secured unanimous approval from the Buena Park City Council for 5600 Beach Blvd, a 13.76-acre residential development in Buena Park. The property is currently occupied by the Amway Corporation with a corporate sale-leaseback in place until the end of 2026 and consists of two industrial buildings totaling approximately 370,031 square feet. “5600 Beach Blvd represents an important step forward for Orange County and is intended to help address the need for attainable and diverse housing options for first-time homebuyers and for Buena Park’s growing senior population,” said Shopoff Realty Investments’ president and CEO, Bill Shopoff. “Transforming an industrial site into a vibrant residential community aligns with the city and county’s evolving needs, providing homes for people at every stage of life.” The development aims to deliver 231 three-story townhomes and duplex units, offered with four different floor plans, along with 50 for-rent senior affordable housing units. Homes are expected to be delivered in 2029-2030. The post Shopoff Secures Approval for Buena Park Residential Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Shopoff Realty secures unanimous approval, 5600 Beach Blvd, Buena Park; 231 townhomes + 50 senior units
13.76-acre Amway site conversion; sale-leaseback through end 2026; delivery 2029–2030
281-unit residential development (mixed-income townhomes and affordable senior housing)
stories.summary: Shopoff Realty Investments secured unanimous approval from Buena Park City Council to develop 5600 Beach Blvd, a 13.76-acre former Amway corporate site, into 281 residential units comprising 231 three-story townhomes/duplexes and 50 for-rent affordable senior units. Amway sale-leaseback expires end of 2026; deliveries expected 2029–2030. The mixed-income development targets first-time homebuyers and seniors.
stories.impact: Significant entitlement win in Orange County. Unanimous City Council approval removes entitlement risk and validates municipal appetite for industrial-to-residential conversion in Buena Park; signals shift in demand from logistics/manufacturing to housing. Developers should monitor Buena Park, Santa Ana, and broader OC industrial-zoned sites for similar conversion opportunities through 2026–2027, as expiration of legacy corporate leasebacks creates windows for residential redevelopment in underserved southern OC submarkets.

stories.title: Matawan Retail Trades to Private Investor for $15M
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap completed the sale of Park Plaza, a retail center in Matawan, NJ. The asset sold for $14.67 million. “Park Plaza attracted significant investor interest due to its diverse tenant mix, strong visibility and strategic location within one of Monmouth County’s most established retail corridors,” said Seth Goldberg, associate director investments in Marcus & Millichap’s New Jersey office. “Well-positioned neighborhood shopping centers with durable cash flow continue to be highly sought after, and this transaction reflects the sustained demand for quality retail assets in New Jersey.” Goldberg, Brent Hyldahl and Alan Cafiero of Marcus & Millichap marketed the property for the seller and procured the buyer, both private investors from New Jersey. Located at 343-351 State Rte. 34, the retail center sits on a 5.86-acre lot totaling 61,750 square feet. It was built in 1986 and contains 20 suites. The rent roll features a diverse mix of dining, lifestyle, retail and service-oriented tenants, including a Dunkin’ with a drive-thru. The post Matawan Retail Trades to Private Investor for $15M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap closes Park Plaza, Matawan NJ retail sale, $14.67M
61,750 SF retail center, 20 suites, 1986-built; diverse tenant mix includes Dunkin'
Strong investor demand for neighborhood shopping centers with durable cash flow in Monmouth County
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap completed the sale of Park Plaza, a 61,750-square-foot retail center in Matawan, NJ (343–351 State Route 34), to a private investor for $14.67 million. Built in 1986, the property contains 20 suites with a diverse mix of dining, lifestyle, retail, and service tenants. The transaction reflects sustained retail-investment demand in established Monmouth County corridors.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. However, sustained investor appetite for neighborhood retail on Route 34 in Monmouth County signals continued suburban consumption and population stability; this corroborates demand for workforce/middle-income multifamily in northern NJ suburbs, particularly around established retail corridors with traffic generation and accessibility.

stories.title: Longfellow Sells Hatch Life Sciences Building in LIC for $87M
stories.excerpt: Life sciences developer Longfellow Real Estate Partners has parted with its first-ever New York City project at a discount. Longfellow’s Hatch Life Sciences Building, located at 43-10 23 Street in Long Island City, Queens, has sold for $86.9 million, according to city records filed Friday. Pearl Realty Management’s Jack Guttman signed for the buyer, under the entity 4310 23 St. A representative of Pearl Realty Management did not respond to requests for comment. Longfellow purchased the existing building at 43-10 23 Street in 2021 alongside its partner, Steven Orbuch’s Sculptor Real Estate, for $92.5 million. Longfellow, led by CEO and co-founder Adam Sichol, planned to invest another $120 million into turning the former parachute manufacturing plant into a mix of life sciences labs and offices. Construction had all but wrapped up when Commercial Observer visited in 2024. The final product spanned over 208,000 square feet across seven floors, including prebuilt lab suites, modular research space and flexible office areas. Longfellow and Sculptor did not respond immediately to requests for comment on the sale. While Guttman’s plans for the purchase remain unclear, the landlord appears to be active in the Long Island City market. Recent purchases include the Standard Motors Product Building at 37-18 Northern Boulevard for $42 million and BrightSpire Capital‘s office building at 21-02 49th Avenue for $28 million. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Longfellow Real Estate sells Hatch Life Sciences Bldg, LIC Queens, for $86.9M
2021 acquisition price: $92.5M (with Sculptor Real Estate); planned $120M renovation
208K SF life sciences campus, 7 floors; sale signals soft NYC lab/creative office market
stories.summary: Longfellow Real Estate Partners sold its Hatch Life Sciences Building at 43–10 23 Street in Long Island City, Queens, for $86.9 million—a discount from its $92.5 million 2021 acquisition price (alongside partner Sculptor Real Estate). Longfellow had planned a $120 million renovation of the former parachute manufacturing plant into 208,000 SF of prebuilt lab suites, modular research space, and flexible office across seven floors. The buyer, Pearl Realty Management, acquired through entity 4310 23 St.
stories.impact: Warning signal for multifamily developers in Long Island City / Queens. The life sciences building sale at a loss—despite proximity to transit and completed construction—reflects softening demand for specialized office/lab space in LIC and signals potential tenant weakness in the broader creative/tech office category. Multifamily developers should scrutinize near-term employment stability in LIC/Queens and underwrite conservatively for sustained rental demand, particularly if lab/office conversions falter; monitor whether this asset cycles to alternative uses (e.g., residential conversion, flex workspace) that could augment housing supply.

stories.title: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Buys Two Miami Affordable Housing Rentals
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management has acquired two affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County from the Gatehouse Group, paying a combined $63.8 million, property records show. In the largest deal, the investor paid $34 million for the 150-unit Magnolia Landing Apartments in the Naranja neighborhood, near the southern end of the county. Built in 2011, the 4.8-acre asset houses 20 three-story buildings at 25881 Southwest 143rd Court, just west of the South Dixie Highway. The sale breaks down to roughly $226,660 per unit. CBRE Capital Partners provided a $23.8 million Freddie Mac loan. Across the county in Miami’s Little River neighborhood, Starwood paid $29.75 million for the 160-unit Lafayette Square complex. The 19-story building sits on a 1.2-acre site, a block west from Northeast Second Avenue at 150 Northeast 79th Street. The deal equates to about $185,900 per apartment. The Gatehouse Group appears to have retained ownership of the adjacent 136-unit property. The Mansfield, Mass.-based firm developed both the Lafayette Square and Magnolia Landing Apartments, completing the former in 2008 and the latter in 2011. Representatives for Starwood and Gatehouse Group did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Asset Management (Sternlicht) acquires two Miami affordable housing rentals, $63.8M combined
Magnolia Landing (150 units, Naranja): $34M; Lafayette Square (160 units, Little River): $29.75M
Freddie Mac financing ($23.8M on Magnolia); strong investor appetite for affordable Miami rentals
stories.summary: Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Asset Management acquired two affordable housing properties from Gatehouse Group for a combined $63.8 million in Miami-Dade County. Magnolia Landing (150 units, Naranja, built 2011) sold for $34 million ($226,660/unit); Lafayette Square (160 units, Little River, 19-story) for $29.75 million ($185,900/unit). CBRE Capital Partners arranged a $23.8 million Freddie Mac loan for Magnolia.
stories.impact: Strong acquisition signal for Miami-Dade affordable multifamily. A major institutional investor (Sternlicht/Starwood) deploying $63.8M into existing affordable stock—despite older vintages—suggests confidence in Miami-Dade rental fundamentals, particularly in southern and central neighborhoods (Naranja, Little River). Developers should view this as validation of persistent demand for workforce/affordable rental product in Miami-Dade; counter-cyclical institutional buying at lower unit economics indicates cap rates/yields remain attractive, supporting development feasibility for new affordable/mixed-income projects in underserved southern-county and Little River submarkets.

stories.title: Ad Agency Doubles Office HQ Space in Move to Hackman Campus in L.A.
stories.excerpt: An international advertising agency is more than doubling its office footprint with a new headquarters lease in El Segundo, Calif. Innocean USA signed the 101,000-square-foot deal at Hackman Capital Partners’ creative office campus in the small enclave just south of Los Angeles International Airport. The agency will relocate nearly 600 employees from 50,000 square feet in Huntington Beach after construction on its new space concludes in 2027, according to JLL, which represented the tenant. The company reportedly will use part of the space as a production facility for commercials and other content. Terms of the lease were not disclosed. “This move is about creating the right environment for our next chapter,” Innocean USA CEO Steve Jun said in a statement. “This is an investment in our people, our clients, and the future we’re building together.” The complex, named after its address at 888 Douglas Street, includes four buildings totaling 550,000 square feet over 30 acres. Hackman acquired the former Northrop Grumman aerospace manufacturing complex in 2016, and invested about $100 million converting it into the creative office. Other major occupiers at the property have included L’Oréal USA, which signed for more than 100,000 square feet in 2021, and Beyond Meat, which originally leased 280,000 square feet for its headquarters. Aerospace and defense companies have also returned to L.A.’s South Bay, and helped bolster leasing at the El Segundo campus. Hypersonic aircraft developer Hermeus signed for 62,552 square feet earlier this year, while Varda Space Industries expanded to 54,749 square feet in 2025. Innocean USA is the U.S. arm of Innocean Worldwide, which was created by Hyundai Motor Group. JLL’s Jason Fine, Jeff Ingham and Mitch Lundquist represented Innocean, while Hackman was represented in-house. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Innocean USA HQ move: 101K SF at 888 Douglas, El Segundo; ~600 employee relocation
Doubling footprint from 50K SF Huntington Beach; move-in 2027
Hackman Capital 30-acre creative campus tenant anchor validates market positioning
stories.summary: International advertising agency Innocean USA signed a 101,000-square-foot lease at Hackman Capital Partners' 888 Douglas creative office campus in El Segundo, doubling its footprint and relocating approximately 600 employees from 50,000 square feet in Huntington Beach. The company will move in after construction concludes in 2027 and use part of the space for commercial production. The complex spans 30 acres and 550,000 square feet over four buildings.
stories.impact: Duplicate of article [2]; same demand signal. Innocean's 600-employee relocation to El Segundo (2027) drives multifamily rental demand in South Bay LAX-adjacent corridor; developers should target mixed-income and upscale workforce housing near 888 Douglas, airport, and Huntington Beach feeder corridors, with completion windows aligned to Q4 2026–Q2 2027 tenant move-in.

stories.title: Attorney James Allen Joins Camber Property Group as Senior Counsel
stories.excerpt: Camber Property Group has onboarded a new general counsel for its affordable housing and community development transactions, Commercial Observer has learned. James Allen has decamped from real estate law firm Hirschen Singer & Epstein and started the new role this week assisting Camber with affordable housing projects in New York state and the New York tri-state region, according to the development firm. “One trend I am seeing is that, in their efforts to solve the ongoing housing affordability crisis, more developers are starting to expand both the types of projects that they participate in and their geographic footprint,” Allen said in a statement. “Camber is always thinking creatively about both, but they present unique challenges.” Allen was previously an associate for four years at Nixon Peabody and a senior staff attorney for the New York Court of Appeals. The Brooklyn Law School graduate also pens articles about housing equity and affordability while serving on the board of the New York Housing Conference’s Rising Leaders Network and the New York City Bar Association’s Housing & Urban Development Committee. Hirschen Singer & Epstein did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “I feel lucky to have the chance to expand upon that and work with many of the legal partners that I have learned from over the years, while Camber solidifies its New York presence and intentionally expands its footprint to other regions,” Allen said. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: James Allen joins Camber Property Group as Senior Counsel for affordable housing/community development
Focus: NY state and tri-state affordable housing transactions and complex entitlements
Trend: Developers expanding project types and geographic footprint in affordable housing
stories.summary: Camber Property Group hired James Allen as General Counsel to lead affordable housing and community development transactions across New York state and the tri-state region. Allen, previously at Hirschen Singer & Epstein and Nixon Peabody, noted an industry trend toward developers expanding project types and geographic scope to address housing affordability. He also serves on the NY Housing Conference's Rising Leaders Network and NYC Bar Association housing committees.
stories.impact: Hiring trend signal for multifamily development landscape. Camber's expansion of in-house legal/transactions counsel focused on affordable housing suggests the developer is scaling mixed-income and affordable projects across tri-state; this reflects broader industry shift (acknowledged by Allen) toward developer geographic and product diversification. For multifamily peers, this signals growing competition for affordable/mixed-income deals in NY/tri-state and highlights importance of in-house expertise in complex affordable housing structures (LIHTC, Section 8, community land trusts, affordability covenants) to compete for capital and entitlements.

stories.title: Selldorf Architects Renews 14K-SF 860 Broadway Lease for 10 Years
stories.excerpt: Architecture firm Selldorf Architects has renewed its 10-year, 13,815-square-foot lease at Gordon Property Group’s 860 Broadway. Selldorf has called the Flatiron District’s 860 Broadway home for the last two decades, according to landlord brokerage Colliers. The asking rent was not disclosed. However, the average asking rent for office space in Midtown South was $79.41 per square foot, with Class A office space asking an average of $97.22 per foot and Class B space asking $79.96 during the second quarter, according to Colliers data. Seth Hecht from Colliers represented Gordon Property in this deal, while the tenant was represented by Erik Schmall and Scott Weiss from Savills. “860 Broadway is one of Manhattan’s iconic office buildings, and its location continues to make it a highly desirable destination for creative and innovative companies,” Hecht said in a statement announcing the renewal. “When a firm as globally respected as Selldorf Architects commits to another decade in the building, it speaks to both the property’s enduring appeal and the long-term strength of this market.” Savills did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment. “Our focus has always been on owning and operating buildings for the long term,” Tim Gordon, managing director of Gordon Property Group, said in the statement. “Creating an environment where great companies choose to stay and grow is the ultimate measure of our success, and we’re proud that 860 Broadway continues to earn that kind of commitment.” Selldorf Architects was founded by Annabelle Selldorf in New York City in 1988, according to the company website. The firm has worked on a number of prestigious projects, including the Frick Collection, the Chateau Haut-Brion — a 16th century estate near Bordeaux in France – and the Museum of Contemporary Art in San Diego. bullets: Selldorf Architects renews 13,815 SF lease, 860 Broadway Manhattan, 10-year term
Two-decade tenant commitment; Flatiron District office market sustained creative-class demand
Class A/B Midtown South asking rents: $79.41 avg., Class A $97.22/SF (Q2)
stories.summary: Architecture firm Selldorf Architects renewed its 10-year lease for 13,815 square feet at 860 Broadway in Manhattan's Flatiron District, where it has been a tenant for 20 years. The renewal was brokered by Colliers (landlord) and Savills (tenant). Midtown South office average asking rent was $79.41/SF in Q2 (Class A: $97.22/SF; Class B: $79.96/SF). Asking rent for this renewal was not disclosed.
stories.impact: Duplicate of article [1]; minimal direct relevance. Office lease renewal underscores stability of Manhattan's design/creative-class employment base and validates Flatiron/NoMad as premium office destination; trailing indicator of sustained professional services and design sector health, which supports resident base and discretionary spending in adjacent residential neighborhoods, but is not a leading demand signal for new multifamily supply.
